how_to_obtain.expected_output: A completed mapping showing 100% of sensitive operations with corresponding role checks = 'full'. Gaps in coverage = 'partial'. No role checks documented = 'none'.

typical_values: partial (most common - delete operations protected but export/admin-config missed)
full (security-mature applications with comprehensive threat modeling)

option_description: Controls whether the default or standard user role explicitly excludes permissions for destructive and sensitive operations (delete, export, admin-config), enforcing a clear privilege boundary between standard and privileged roles in the permission matrix.
security_impact: The Rego rule `privileged_action_prevention_coverage` requires this to be true. Without explicit privilege separation, permission inheritance or overly broad role definitions may inadvertently grant standard users access to sensitive operations. Explicit denial or non-assignment enforces the principle of least privilege and limits the impact of compromised standard user accounts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the role permission matrix or policy files to confirm the standard/default user role does not include delete, export, or admin-config permissions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Standard user role permissions list containing only read/create operations without delete, export, bulk, or admin actions confirms true. Presence of those actions confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Authenticate as a standard (non-admin) user and attempt to perform privileged actions, verifying they are denied at the authorization layer.
how_to_obtain.command: STANDARD_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://app.example.com/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"standard@test.com","password":"testpass"}' | jq -r '.access_token'); echo 'Delete test:'; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $STANDARD_TOKEN" https://app.example.com/api/records/1; echo; echo 'Export test:'; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $STANDARD_TOKEN" https://app.example.com/api/export/all; echo
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 403 returned for both delete and export attempts confirms true. HTTP 200 or 404 (resource not found but no auth rejection) confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the application admin console, navigate to the standard user role definition and review its permission set for the presence of any destructive or sensitive operation permissions.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console → Roles → Standard User / Default Role → Permissions tab → Verify no 'Delete', 'Export', 'Bulk Operations', or 'Admin Config' permissions are checked or assigned
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Standard user role showing only read/write permissions without destructive operations confirms true.

typical_values: true (applications with explicit deny-by-default permission models)
false (flat RBAC models where standard users inherit broad permissions)

option_description: Controls whether the application automatically synchronizes role assignments from an authoritative identity provider (LDAP, SCIM, Azure AD, Okta, etc.) rather than relying solely on manual role management within the application.
security_impact: The Rego rule `integration_with_identity_provider` requires this to be true. Without IdP sync, role assignments can become stale — employees who change roles or leave the organization may retain application access indefinitely. Automated synchronization ensures role memberships reflect the authoritative HR/directory state and enables prompt access revocation when users are offboarded.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the application's identity provider integration configuration file or environment variables for SCIM, LDAP, or directory sync settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Variables like `SCIM_ENABLED=true`, `LDAP_SYNC_ENABLED=true`, or a non-empty `LDAP_HOST` with sync configuration present confirms true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the application's SSO/directory integration settings in the admin console to verify whether SCIM provisioning or directory sync is actively enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console → Security → Identity Provider / SSO Settings → Provisioning tab → Check SCIM Provisioning toggle or Directory Sync status | Okta Admin → Applications → [App] → Provisioning → To App → Enable Create/Update/Deactivate Users
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Provisioning or sync toggle showing 'Enabled' or 'Active' confirms true. Disabled or absent provisioning settings confirms false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the application's SCIM endpoint or admin API to verify whether an active IdP integration with provisioning capabilities is configured.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' https://app.example.com/api/v1/admin/integrations | jq '.[] | select(.type == "scim" or .type == "ldap") | {type: .type, enabled: .enabled, last_sync: .last_sync_at}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integration object with `enabled: true` and a recent `last_sync_at` timestamp confirms true. No integration objects or `enabled: false` confirms false.

typical_values: true (enterprise SaaS applications with SSO requirements)
false (SMB deployments, self-hosted applications, or applications relying on manual user management)

option_description: Specifies how often (in minutes) the application polls or receives updates from the identity provider to synchronize role memberships. A value of 0 indicates real-time or push-based synchronization (e.g., SCIM webhooks). Lower values reduce the window during which stale or revoked permissions remain active.
security_impact: The Rego rule `integration_with_identity_provider` requires this value to be 1440 minutes (24 hours) or less, with 0 being ideal for push-based sync. High sync intervals create windows where terminated employees or role-changed users retain incorrect application permissions. A 10080-minute (7-day) sync interval means a terminated user could retain access for a full week.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IdP sync scheduler configuration, cron job definitions, or SCIM polling interval settings to determine the synchronization frequency.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Variables like `LDAP_SYNC_INTERVAL=60` (minutes) or cron expression `*/60 * * * *` reveals the sync frequency in minutes. Push-based SCIM will show no polling interval or interval=0.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the IdP integration settings panel in the application admin console or the identity provider's provisioning configuration for the sync schedule.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console → Identity Provider Settings → Sync Schedule → Review polling interval | Azure AD → Enterprise Applications → [App] → Provisioning → Settings → Provisioning Interval | Okta → Applications → [App] → Provisioning → Integration → API polling interval
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A displayed interval value (e.g., '60 minutes', 'Every hour', 'Real-time') provides the sync frequency. Record the value in minutes (real-time = 0).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review application or IdP integration logs to measure the actual interval between consecutive sync events, which reveals the effective sync frequency.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i 'ldap sync\|scim sync\|directory sync\|user sync' /var/log/app/application.log | tail -20 | awk '{print $1, $2}' | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Consecutive sync log entries with timestamps allow calculation of the actual interval in minutes between synchronizations.

option_description: Defines the automated action taken on a user's application role assignments when that user is removed or disabled in the identity provider. Options are 'immediate_revocation' (roles removed instantly), 'deactivate_account' (account disabled but roles preserved), 'manual_review' (a workflow is triggered for human review), or 'no_action' (application takes no automated action).
security_impact: The Rego rule `integration_with_identity_provider` requires this value to be either 'immediate_revocation' or 'deactivate_account'. The 'no_action' option is the most dangerous, as terminated employees or compromised accounts removed from the IdP would retain full application access indefinitely. 'manual_review' creates a window of exposure between IdP removal and application role revocation. 'immediate_revocation' provides the tightest security posture.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the SCIM provisioning or IdP integration configuration for the deprovisioning or offboarding action setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration values like `DEPROVISION_ACTION=immediate_revocation`, `deactivate_on_remove: true`, or SCIM delete action set to 'deactivate' identify the configured behavior.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the identity provider integration provisioning settings and review the action configured for user removal or deprovisioning.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console → Security → SSO/SCIM → Provisioning → Deprovisioning Actions → Review 'When users are removed from IdP' setting | Okta → Applications → [App] → Provisioning → To App → Deprovisioning → Review Deactivate or Sync Password | Azure AD → Enterprise Apps → [App] → Provisioning → Settings → Scope → Review deprovisioning behavior
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Setting showing 'Deactivate account', 'Revoke access immediately', or 'Remove roles' confirms acceptable values. 'Do nothing' or absence of deprovisioning config confirms 'no_action'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the IT administrator or review the offboarding runbook to determine what happens in the application when a user is terminated and removed from the IdP.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented automated process that immediately revokes or deactivates confirms 'immediate_revocation' or 'deactivate_account'. Absence of automated process or manual-only steps confirms 'manual_review' or 'no_action'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review application access logs or provisioning event logs after a known test-user removal from the IdP to observe what action was automatically taken.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries showing immediate role removal or account deactivation upon IdP user deletion confirm 'immediate_revocation' or 'deactivate_account'. No log entries or manual-only entries confirm 'no_action' or 'manual_review'.

typical_values: deactivate_account (most common in enterprise SaaS defaults)

option_description: Controls whether a formal, documented periodic role review and recertification process exists for RBAC assignments. When enabled, it confirms that a structured workflow is in place to periodically validate that all user-to-role mappings remain appropriate and authorized.
security_impact: The Rego policy for role_review_and_recertification requires this attribute to be true as a prerequisite condition before the countermeasure can fire. Without a defined review process, accumulated entitlements and orphaned permissions go undetected indefinitely, exposing the organization to privilege creep. This is the foundational gate that enables all downstream recertification logic in the policy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Log into SailPoint IdentityNow or Saviynt and navigate to the Access Reviews or Certification Campaigns section. Verify that at least one active or scheduled campaign definition exists targeting RBAC role assignments.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SailPoint IdentityNow: Admin > Access Reviews > Campaigns | Saviynt: Dashboard > Access Certification > Campaigns
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one campaign with a recurring schedule and defined reviewer ownership is present and in Active or Scheduled status.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SailPoint IdentityNow API to retrieve all certification campaigns and check for at least one campaign in an active or scheduled state targeting role assignments.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com/v3/campaigns?filters=type eq "MANAGER"' | jq '[.[] | select(.status == "ACTIVE" or .status == "STAGED")]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON array containing one or more campaign objects with status ACTIVE or STAGED, confirming a review process is operational.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the IAM team or access governance owner to confirm whether a written role recertification policy exists. Request documentation such as a process runbook, governance policy document, or ITSM change record that defines recertification obligations.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A policy document or runbook is produced that defines recertification triggers, reviewer responsibilities, and escalation procedures.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review IAM platform audit logs or ITSM ticket history for completed access review campaigns within the past 12 months to confirm the process has been executed, not just defined.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries showing completed certification campaigns with timestamps, confirming the process is actively executed.

option_description: Defines the maximum allowable number of days between mandatory role assignment review and recertification cycles. This integer value sets the cadence at which all in-scope role assignments must be reviewed, with common intervals being 90 (quarterly), 180 (semi-annual), or 365 (annual).
security_impact: The Rego policy checks that review_frequency_days is less than or equal to 365 for the role_review_and_recertification countermeasure to satisfy. A longer interval means permission drift persists for a longer window before correction. Organizations targeting stronger access governance should set this to 90 or 180, aligning with quarterly or semi-annual reviews to limit the exposure window for stale or unauthorized role assignments.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open SailPoint IdentityNow or Saviynt and inspect the configuration of the most recent or active certification campaign. Look for the campaign duration, deadline, or recurrence interval setting to determine the configured review cycle length.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SailPoint IdentityNow: Admin > Access Reviews > Campaigns > [Campaign Name] > Settings > Duration | Saviynt: Access Certification > Campaigns > [Campaign] > Schedule
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric duration value (in days) displayed for the campaign, such as 90, 180, or 365, representing the review cycle interval.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve campaign details from SailPoint IdentityNow API and extract the deadline or duration field to compute the configured recurrence frequency in days.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON output listing each campaign's name, creation date, and deadline, from which the review interval in days can be calculated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the organization's IAM governance policy or access control standard document to identify the formally mandated recertification frequency. Cross-reference with ITSM calendar entries or scheduled task configurations for IAM automation jobs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented policy statement such as 'Role recertification shall occur no less than quarterly (every 90 days)' with associated scheduling evidence.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If IAM tooling is self-hosted, inspect the campaign scheduler configuration file or database configuration for the recertification job interval setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A configuration key-value pair such as 'review_interval_days: 90' confirming the programmatic schedule for review campaigns.

option_description: Represents the number of days elapsed since the most recently completed role recertification cycle concluded. This is a computed or observed value derived by finding the completion date of the last closed campaign and calculating the difference from today's date.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires last_review_completed_days_ago to be less than or equal to 365 for the role_review_and_recertification countermeasure to activate. If this value exceeds the configured review_frequency_days threshold, it signals that the recertification process has lapsed, leaving potentially stale or unauthorized role assignments unreviewed. A large elapsed value indicates the review process, even if defined, is not being executed on schedule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SailPoint IdentityNow API for campaigns with status COMPLETED, sort by most recent completion date, and compute the elapsed days from today.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com/v3/campaigns?filters=status eq "COMPLETED"&sorters=-modified&limit=1' | jq '.[0] | {name: .name, completed: .modified}' && echo "Today: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The most recently completed campaign name and its completion date, from which days elapsed can be computed by subtracting from today's date.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the completed campaigns list in SailPoint, Saviynt, or your IAM platform. Sort by completion date descending and record the date of the most recently closed campaign, then calculate the number of days since that date.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SailPoint IdentityNow: Admin > Access Reviews > Campaigns > Filter: Status = Completed > Sort: End Date Descending | Saviynt: Access Certification > Campaigns > Completed Tab
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list entry showing the most recent campaign with a completion date, e.g., 'Q3 2024 Role Review - Completed: 2024-09-30', from which elapsed days are calculated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search IAM platform audit logs for the most recent campaign completion event and extract the timestamp, then compute elapsed days using shell arithmetic or a script.
how_to_obtain.command: awk '/campaign.*complet/I {ts=$1" "$2; found=1} END {if(found) print ts}' /var/log/iam/audit.log | xargs -I{} bash -c 'echo $(( ($(date +%s) - $(date -d "{}" +%s)) / 86400 )) days ago'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric output such as '47 days ago' indicating how many days have elapsed since the last review was completed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Ask the IAM team or access governance owner to provide the sign-off date or closure report for the most recent recertification campaign. Review any emailed campaign completion notifications or ITSM closure tickets.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A dated document, email notification, or ITSM ticket closure record confirming the last campaign completed on a specific date, from which elapsed days can be manually computed.

option_description: Indicates whether the role recertification workflow enforces actual removal of role assignments when a reviewer denies or rejects an assignment during a review campaign. This means a 'revoke' decision must trigger automated or trackable deprovisioning of the role, not merely log a disagreement without follow-through.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires revocation_action_supported to be true as a co-condition alongside role_review_process_enabled for the role_review_and_recertification countermeasure to fire. Without enforced revocation, the recertification process becomes a paper exercise: reviewers may deny access but unauthorized role assignments persist in the system. This attribute validates that the review loop is closed and access removals are operationally enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SailPoint IdentityNow or Saviynt, open an active or completed certification campaign and inspect the reviewer decision options. Verify that selecting 'Revoke' or 'Deny' for an assignment triggers an automated provisioning action (deprovisioning request) rather than simply flagging the record.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SailPoint IdentityNow: Admin > Access Reviews > Campaigns > [Campaign] > Reviewer Decisions > Revoke Action Configuration | Saviynt: Access Certification > Campaign Settings > Remediation Actions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A configured remediation action is shown for revoke/deny decisions, such as 'Trigger Provisioning Plan: Remove Role Assignment' or 'Create Deprovisioning Task', confirming automated enforcement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query SailPoint IdentityNow for certification reviewer decisions with revoke status and verify that corresponding provisioning actions or work items were generated as a result.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com/v3/certifications/<certificationId>/reviewer-decisions?filters=decision eq "REVOKE"' | jq '.[] | {item: .id, decision: .decision, remediationCompleted: .remediationCompleted}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Decision records showing decision: REVOKE with remediationCompleted: true or an associated provisioning task ID, confirming revocations are actioned.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the IAM operations team to confirm whether revoke decisions from campaign reviewers automatically generate deprovisioning tickets or provisioning plans in the IAM system. Request a sample workflow trace showing a revoke decision followed by role removal confirmation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence such as a screenshot, workflow diagram, or ITSM ticket chain showing that a reviewer's revoke decision resulted in confirmed role removal from the user's account.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review IAM provisioning logs or audit trails to find instances where a campaign revoke decision was followed by a corresponding role removal event within a reasonable processing window, confirming enforcement is occurring.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries pairing a revoke decision event with a subsequent role removal or deprovisioning confirmation event, demonstrating the enforcement chain is functional.

option_description: Describes the breadth of users and roles covered by the recertification process. Valid values range from 'none' (no review conducted), 'partial' (ad-hoc or incomplete coverage), 'privileged_only' (reviews limited to high-privilege roles), to 'all_roles' (comprehensive coverage of every role and user in scope).
security_impact: While the Rego policy for role_review_and_recertification does not gate directly on review_scope, this attribute provides critical contextual evidence about the quality and completeness of the review process. A scope of 'partial' or 'privileged_only' means standard user role drift goes undetected, leaving a significant surface area of uncertified entitlements. Achieving 'all_roles' maximizes the preventive control value of recertification and closes gaps that attackers could exploit through accumulated standard user permissions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the campaign configuration in SailPoint IdentityNow or Saviynt and review the campaign scope or population settings. Check whether the campaign targets all identities and all roles, specific populations (e.g., only admins), or specific role types.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SailPoint IdentityNow: Admin > Access Reviews > Campaigns > [Campaign] > Scope > Included Identities and Access Items | Saviynt: Access Certification > Campaign > Scope Settings > Users and Roles Included
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Scope configuration showing either 'All Identities + All Roles' (maps to all_roles), 'All Identities + Privileged Roles Only' (maps to privileged_only), a filtered subset (maps to partial), or no campaign (maps to none).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve campaign filter and scope configuration from the SailPoint IdentityNow API to determine what population of users and access items is included in the certification campaign.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com/v3/campaigns/<campaignId>' | jq '{name: .name, type: .type, filter: .filter, accessConstraints: .accessConstraints}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON output showing accessConstraints or filter fields. Empty or null constraints indicate all_roles; constraints scoped to privileged or high-risk roles indicate privileged_only; partial population filters indicate partial.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the IAM governance team or access review campaign owner to determine whether the recertification campaign covers all users across all application roles, or whether certain user populations, role types, or applications are excluded from review cycles.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A clear description of inclusion/exclusion criteria for the review, such as 'We review all roles for all users annually' (all_roles) or 'We only review admin and elevated roles' (privileged_only).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Analyze completed campaign reports or exported review results to count distinct roles and users reviewed versus total role assignments in the environment. A significant gap between reviewed assignments and total assignments indicates partial or privileged_only scope.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com/v3/certifications?campaignId=<id>&limit=250' | jq 'length' && curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' 'https://<tenant>.api.identitynow.com/v3/entitlements?count=true' -I | grep 'X-Total-Count'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Two counts: total certifications reviewed and total entitlements/role assignments in the environment. If reviewed count approximates total count, scope is all_roles; significant gap indicates partial or privileged_only.
